annotations.text:
DIRECTION A — SHELF

Covers lead. The flat 102px text menu on Home is gone: the library IS the home screen, with a persistent 4-item bottom nav.

Data is present but quiet — one score chip, one status chip, one "54 / 213 chapters" line. Nothing competes with the cover art.

Tradeoff: least new data plumbing, least new information. Closest to what ships today, so the cheapest to build.

DIRECTION B — DOSSIER

Data leads. Home becomes a Today screen: the four stat tiles and the 18-week activity heatmap the web dashboard already computes, then Continue, then MAL recommendations.

Library is a dense 194px list row — score, status, genres, download size, chapters read, next chapter — all on one line each.

Tradeoff: needs the most new data on-device, and more full refreshes. Highest payoff for the tracking work.

E-INK GROUND RULES BOTH DIRECTIONS FOLLOW

Drawn at the real panel size: 1264 x 1680 (Libra Colour).

All geometry is lifted from the current source, not invented:
  row height 102px, body text 45px, pad 19px
  title rules #555555, row separators #DDDDDD, card borders #AAAAAA
  progress fill #222222 on a #CCCCCC track, shelf gap 16 / title 44 / bar 8
  DejaVu Sans, regular and bold only — there is no weight scale

No gradients, no shadows, no rounded corners, no anti-aliased hairlines — flat fills and 1px rules only, so partial refresh stays clean and nothing ghosts.

Every tap target is at least 88px tall.

Color is Kaleido: roughly half the saturation of an LCD, and only worth spending on cover art. The one accent (default #B4633A, the web app's warm manga-ink orange) appears only as the nav underline, the score star, and the Continue label — it degrades to a mid-gray gracefully.

HONEST NOTE — THE DATA ISN'T ON THE DEVICE YET

Both mockups show MAL score, rank, status, genres and chapter counts. The device stores none of that today.

SeriesRef (gideon-core/src/series.rs) holds only: source_id, source_name, manga_id, manga_title, cover_url, downloaded map. No genres, no status, no score, no total chapter count.

mal.rs parses ONLY title and cover_url out of the Jikan payload — mean score, status, genres, rank, chapter count all arrive over the wire and get discarded by parse_popular.

Progress is per-chapter only (current_page, total_pages, last_read_at). There is no streak, no pages-read total, no per-day history — computeStats in web/app.js derives all of that from Supabase, on the web side only.

So Direction B's stat band and heatmap need either a stats store on device or a pull from Supabase; Direction A's chips need only the MAL fields mal.rs is already throwing away. That difference is the real cost gap between the two.
